questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.objective: 4.1 Accessing and navigating the Chart of Accounts
questions.keyword: Chart of Accounts navigation path
questions.text: A new bookkeeper needs to find the Chart of Accounts in QuickBooks Online. They are not sure where to access it. Which of the following is a valid navigation path to the Chart of Accounts in QBO?

answers.text: Gear icon > Your Company > Chart of Accounts
+New > Other > Chart of Accounts
Left navigation bar > Banking > Chart of Accounts
Left navigation bar > Reports > Chart of Accounts

explanations.a: Correct — the Chart of Accounts can be accessed via the Gear icon > Your Company > Chart of Accounts, or via the left navigation bar Accounting tab.
explanations.b: The +New menu contains transaction shortcuts only; the Chart of Accounts is not accessible from there.
explanations.c: The Banking tab in the left navigation bar opens the Banking Center for bank feeds, not the Chart of Accounts.
explanations.d: The Reports tab lists available reports; the Chart of Accounts is not a report accessible from that tab.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: four product service types
questions.text: When creating a new product or service in QuickBooks Online, a user must select one of four types. Choosing the correct type determines how the item behaves on transactions. Which set of options correctly lists all four product/service types in QBO?

answers.text: Inventory, Non-Inventory, Expense, Service
Inventory, Non-Inventory, Service, Bundle
Inventory, Stock, Service, Bundle
Product, Non-Product, Service, Bundle

explanations.a: 'Expense' is not one of the four product/service types in QBO; the correct fourth type is Bundle.
explanations.b: Correct — the four product/service types in QuickBooks Online are Inventory, Non-Inventory, Service, and Bundle.
explanations.c: 'Stock' is not a QBO product type; the correct terms are Inventory and Non-Inventory.
explanations.d: 'Product' and 'Non-Product' are not QBO product type names; the correct terms are Inventory and Non-Inventory.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Bundle item definition
questions.text: A music store sells guitar starter packs that include a guitar, a strap, a tuner, and a case — all sold together as one packaged offering. Which QuickBooks Online product/service type best represents this packaged product on sales forms?

answers.text: Non-Inventory — the items are sold as a group without tracking individual quantities
Bundle — a collection of products and services sold together
Service — the packaging and assembly of the items is treated as a service
Inventory — each component in the pack is a physical product

explanations.a: Non-Inventory is for individual physical products where quantities are not tracked, not for grouped offerings.
explanations.b: Correct — a Bundle is a collection of products and services sold together on a sales form, which fits the guitar starter pack scenario.
explanations.c: Service items represent services provided to customers, not a package of physical goods sold together.
explanations.d: While each component may be an inventory item, the combined package as a whole is set up as a Bundle item in QBO.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: inventory item type subscription restriction
questions.text: A business owner on QuickBooks Online Essentials tries to set up a product and select Inventory as the type to track quantities on hand. They notice the Inventory option appears unavailable. Why is the Inventory type not accessible in Essentials?

answers.text: The Inventory type requires an active Payroll subscription before it can be used
Inventory items are only available after connecting a bank feed in the Banking Center
Inventory items are only available in QuickBooks Online Plus and Advanced subscriptions
The Inventory type is available in all subscriptions but must first be enabled by a Company Admin

explanations.a: A Payroll subscription has no connection to the availability of the Inventory product type.
explanations.b: Connecting a bank feed enables transaction downloads and has no effect on inventory item availability.
explanations.c: Correct — the Inventory product type is only available in QuickBooks Online Plus and Advanced subscriptions, and inventory tracking must also be enabled in Account and Settings.
explanations.d: The Inventory type cannot be enabled in Essentials regardless of the user role; upgrading the subscription is required.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: FIFO definition
questions.text: QuickBooks Online uses a specific method to value inventory and determine the cost of goods sold. A new bookkeeper asks what the acronym FIFO stands for. What does FIFO mean?

answers.text: Final Invoice For Order
Funds In, Funds Out
Fixed Income Financial Operations
First In, First Out

explanations.a: Final Invoice For Order is not the meaning of FIFO in the context of inventory accounting.
explanations.b: Funds In, Funds Out is not the meaning of FIFO; that describes basic cash flow, not inventory costing.
explanations.c: Fixed Income Financial Operations is not the meaning of FIFO in an inventory context.
explanations.d: Correct — FIFO stands for First In, First Out, meaning the oldest inventory items purchased are expensed first when calculating cost of goods sold.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.objective: 4.2 Creating and editing Chart of Accounts
questions.keyword: account numbers enable location
questions.text: A controller wants to assign account numbers to all general ledger accounts in QuickBooks Online to make financial statements easier to reference and organize. They need to know where to enable this feature. Where is the option to turn on account numbers for the Chart of Accounts located?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Advanced tab
Account and Settings > Company tab
Gear icon > Lists > Chart of Accounts settings
Left navigation bar > Accounting > Account Numbers

explanations.a: Correct — the option to turn on account numbers for the Chart of Accounts is found in Account and Settings under the Advanced tab.
explanations.b: The Company tab in Account and Settings contains general company identity information, not chart of accounts settings.
explanations.c: The Gear icon > Lists does not contain a Chart of Accounts settings option for account numbers.
explanations.d: The Accounting tab in the left navigation bar links to Chart of Accounts and Reconcile, but account numbers must be turned on via Account and Settings > Advanced.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.objective: 4.2 Creating and editing Chart of Accounts
questions.keyword: adding a new account in COA
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to add a new income account in QuickBooks Online to track a new revenue stream. After navigating to the Chart of Accounts screen, what action do they take to begin creating the new account?

answers.text: Click New in the top right corner of the Chart of Accounts screen
Click +New in the left navigation bar and select Chart of Accounts entry
Click the small gear icon within the Chart of Accounts and select Add Account
Go to Account and Settings > Advanced and use the Add Account option there

explanations.a: Correct — to add a new account in the Chart of Accounts, click the New button in the top right corner of the Chart of Accounts screen.
explanations.b: The +New button in the left navigation bar is for creating transactions such as invoices and bills, not for adding chart of accounts entries.
explanations.c: The small gear icon within the Chart of Accounts provides display options such as including inactive accounts, not an Add Account option.
explanations.d: Account and Settings > Advanced does not contain an Add Account function; new accounts are created from within the Chart of Accounts screen itself.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Category field groups products for reports
questions.text: When creating a new product in QuickBooks Online, a manager wants to assign it to a named group so that similar products are totaled together on reports and appear grouped in the product list. Which field on the product creation screen serves this purpose?

answers.text: The SKU field, which assigns a stock keeping unit code used for product grouping
The Category field, which places the product into a named Product Category
The Expense Account field, which links the product to a chart of accounts category
The Description field, which can include a grouping tag for report filtering

explanations.a: The SKU field stores a stock keeping unit identifier for the individual product, not a grouping category.
explanations.b: Correct — the Category field on the product/service creation screen assigns the item to a Product Category, which groups similar products for reporting and speeds up data entry.
explanations.c: The Expense Account field maps the product to a chart of accounts line for purchasing purposes, not for grouping products on reports.
explanations.d: The Description field provides text that appears on sales forms; it does not function as a grouping tag for reports.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: two-sided items income and expense account
questions.text: A bookkeeper is creating a product in QuickBooks Online Plus that the company both buys from vendors and sells to customers. They want to map the same item to an income account for sales and an expense account for purchases. What is this feature called, and in which subscriptions is it available?

answers.text: Double-entry mapping — available in all subscription levels of QuickBooks Online
Account pairing — available in Essentials, Plus, and Advanced subscriptions
Two-sided items — available in Plus and Advanced subscriptions only
Dual-account tracking — available in Plus only, not in Advanced

explanations.a: Double-entry mapping is not the QBO term for this feature; it is called two-sided items and is not available in all subscriptions.
explanations.b: Account pairing is not the QBO term, and the feature is not available in Essentials — only Plus and Advanced.
explanations.c: Correct — two-sided items allow one product name to be mapped to an income account when selling and an expense account when buying; this feature is available in Plus and Advanced only.
explanations.d: The feature is called two-sided items and is available in both Plus and Advanced, not Plus only.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Product Categories two purposes
questions.text: A business owner asks their bookkeeper why they should set up Product Categories rather than relying on clear product names alone. According to the Student Guide, what are the two purposes of Product Categories in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: Product Categories lock prices for items in the group and enable bulk discounts
Product Categories activate inventory tracking and auto-generate purchase orders for each category
Product Categories automatically apply the correct tax rate based on the item category
Product Categories total all products of the same category on reports and make data entry faster by grouping items in drop-down menus

explanations.a: Product Categories do not lock prices or enable bulk discounts; those are separate features.
explanations.b: Product Categories do not activate inventory tracking or auto-generate purchase orders.
explanations.c: Product Categories do not automatically apply tax rates; tax settings are configured at the individual product level.
explanations.d: Correct — the Student Guide identifies two purposes of Product Categories: all products in the same category are totaled on reports, and using categories makes data entry faster by grouping items in drop-down menus.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: I sell checkbox required for sales forms
questions.text: A bookkeeper is creating a new inventory item in QuickBooks Online Plus and wants it to appear on customer invoices with a price field. Which checkbox on the product creation screen must be selected to ensure the item and its price fields appear on sales forms?

answers.text: I sell this product/service to my customers
I purchase this product/service from a vendor
Track inventory quantity on hand
Enable this item for customer-facing sales forms

explanations.a: Correct — checking 'I sell this product/service to my customers' ensures that the various sales-related fields, including price and income account, appear on the product record and on sales forms.
explanations.b: 'I purchase this product/service from a vendor' activates the purchasing information section (cost, expense account) for the item but does not affect its appearance on sales forms.
explanations.c: 'Track inventory quantity on hand' is the option for enabling inventory tracking in Account and Settings, not a checkbox on the individual product creation screen for sales form appearance.
explanations.d: 'Enable this item for customer-facing sales forms' is not a checkbox that exists in QuickBooks Online; the correct checkbox is 'I sell this product/service to my customers.'

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: vendor Billing rate field time tracking
questions.text: A subcontractor's vendor record in QuickBooks Online includes a Billing rate field. A bookkeeper asks when this field is used. In what situation is the Billing rate field on a vendor record relevant?

answers.text: It sets the maximum invoice amount the vendor may submit per billing period
It stores the rate that populates time tracking records when tracking billable time for the vendor
It determines the default expense account applied when recording vendor bills
It stores the vendor's preferred discount rate for calculating early payment terms

explanations.a: The Billing rate field does not set an invoice cap; it provides a default rate for time tracking entries.
explanations.b: Correct — the Billing rate field on a vendor record is used when tracking billable time, so the rate can automatically populate time tracking records associated with that vendor.
explanations.c: The expense account assigned to a vendor bill is determined by the category or item selected in the transaction, not the Billing rate field.
explanations.d: Early payment discounts are managed through vendor payment terms, not the Billing rate field.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: SKU field stock keeping unit
questions.text: A retail business is setting up inventory items in QuickBooks Online and asks what the SKU field on the product/service record is used for. What is the purpose of the SKU field?

answers.text: SKU identifies the sales tax category applied to the item on sales forms
SKU is an internal QuickBooks code automatically generated for each new item
SKU allows the business to enter a stock keeping unit code to identify the product
SKU links the item to an external barcode scanner integration within QuickBooks Online

explanations.a: The SKU field does not control tax categories; tax settings are configured separately at the product level.
explanations.b: SKU is not auto-generated by QBO; it is an optional field the user fills in with their own stock keeping unit code.
explanations.c: Correct — the SKU field on a product/service record allows the business to enter a stock keeping unit code to identify the item, typically matching their internal inventory numbering system.
explanations.d: The SKU field stores an identifier string; it does not create or manage an external barcode scanner integration.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: inventory features after enabling
questions.text: A QuickBooks Online Plus user has just enabled inventory tracking via Account and Settings. A colleague asks what specific capabilities become available. Which set of features does the Student Guide describe as part of inventory tracking in QBO?

answers.text: Weighted average cost valuation, reorder point alerts, and automatic purchase order generation
LIFO or FIFO valuation choice, batch inventory adjustments, and vendor-specific pricing
Product expiration date tracking, multi-location inventory, and demand forecasting
Quantity available visible on sales forms, inventory quantity adjustments including batch adjustments, and the Physical Inventory Worksheet report

explanations.a: QBO uses FIFO only (not weighted average), and reorder point alerts and auto-PO generation are not listed as QBO inventory features in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: QBO does not offer a LIFO option; it uses FIFO exclusively, and vendor-specific pricing is not described as an inventory tracking feature.
explanations.c: Product expiration tracking, multi-location inventory, and demand forecasting are not features listed for QBO inventory tracking in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: Correct — the Student Guide lists quantity available on sales forms, inventory adjustments (including batch adjustments to multiple products at once), and the Physical Inventory Worksheet report as the features of inventory tracking.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Non-Inventory for physical products without quantity tracking
questions.text: A wholesale distributor sells physical goods but does not need to track how many units are on hand in QuickBooks Online. Their bookkeeper is setting up the product list. Which product/service type should they use for these physical products?

answers.text: Inventory — because the products are physical goods
Bundle — because the distributor often sells multiple products together
Service — because no quantity tracking is involved
Non-Inventory — for items bought and/or sold where quantity tracking is not needed

explanations.a: Inventory type is for physical goods where the business needs to track quantities on hand; it is not the right choice when quantity tracking is not needed or desired.
explanations.b: Bundle is for selling multiple products and services together as a single packaged offering, not for individual physical goods.
explanations.c: Service is for services provided to customers, not for physical goods sold without quantity tracking.
explanations.d: Correct — Non-Inventory is the appropriate type for physical products that are bought and/or sold but where the business does not need to track quantities on hand.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: inventory tracking enable exact navigation path
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to activate inventory quantity tracking for a client on QuickBooks Online Plus. They know it is somewhere in Account and Settings but cannot find the exact location. What is the precise navigation path to enable inventory tracking?

answers.text: Gear icon > Account and Settings > Sales > Products and Services > Track inventory quantity on hand
Gear icon > Account and Settings > Advanced > Inventory > Enable FIFO Inventory Tracking
Left navigation bar > Accounting > Chart of Accounts > Inventory Settings
Left navigation bar > Sales > Products and Services > Enable Inventory toggle

explanations.a: Correct — to enable inventory tracking, navigate to the Gear icon > Account and Settings > Sales tab > Products and Services section > and check Track inventory quantity on hand.
explanations.b: The Advanced tab does not contain an Inventory section or an Enable FIFO toggle; inventory is enabled in the Sales tab.
explanations.c: The Chart of Accounts does not contain inventory settings; inventory is enabled in Account and Settings.
explanations.d: The Products and Services list in the left navigation bar does not contain an Enable Inventory toggle; the setting is in Account and Settings > Sales.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.objective: 4.2 Creating and editing Chart of Accounts
questions.keyword: Billable expense income account setting Advanced tab
questions.text: A bookkeeper has enabled billable expenses in QuickBooks Online Plus and wants to designate which income account captures revenue when a billable expense is invoiced to a customer. Where in Account and Settings is the Billable expense income account configured?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Expenses tab > Billable Expense Income Account field
Account and Settings > Advanced tab, where the Billable expense income account can be specified
Chart of Accounts — create a new income account and designate it as the default billable income account
Account and Settings > Sales > Products and Services > Billable Income Account selector

explanations.a: The Expenses tab contains settings for enabling billable expenses but does not contain the field to specify which income account captures the billable revenue.
explanations.b: Correct — the Billable expense income account is specified in the Advanced tab of Account and Settings, where you also find related accounting settings.
explanations.c: Creating an income account in the Chart of Accounts does not designate it as the billable expense income account; that designation is made in Account and Settings > Advanced.
explanations.d: The Products and Services section in the Sales tab is for inventory and price settings, not for assigning a billable expense income account.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: late fees enable Sales tab Account and Settings
questions.text: A business owner wants to charge customers late fees on overdue invoices in QuickBooks Online. After enabling late fees globally, the bookkeeper explains that settings can also be customized per customer. Where in Account and Settings is the option to globally turn on late fees first found?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Expenses tab > Late Fees section
Account and Settings > Advanced tab > Late Fee Automation toggle
Account and Settings > Sales tab > Late fees section
Account and Settings > Company tab > Customer Billing Preferences

explanations.a: The Expenses tab manages purchase and bill settings; it does not contain late fee settings for customer invoices.
explanations.b: The Advanced tab contains accounting, automation, and time-tracking settings; the late fees option is not found there.
explanations.c: Correct — late fees can be turned on in Account and Settings > Sales tab, after which individual customer late fee settings can be customized.
explanations.d: The Company tab stores general company information and does not contain a Customer Billing Preferences section with late fee settings.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Price rules enable location Sales tab
questions.text: A business owner wants to set up price rules to offer different pricing tiers for different customer groups in QuickBooks Online. Their bookkeeper needs to know where to turn this feature on. Which section of Account and Settings contains the option to enable price rules?

answers.text: Account and Settings > Advanced tab > Pricing section
Account and Settings > Expenses tab > Price Rules toggle
Account and Settings > Sales tab > Products and Services section
Account and Settings > Company tab > Price Management section

explanations.a: The Advanced tab contains automation, accounting method, and time-tracking settings; it does not have a Pricing section for price rules.
explanations.b: The Expenses tab manages purchase and bill settings; it does not contain a Price Rules toggle.
explanations.c: Correct — price rules can be turned on in the Account and Settings > Sales tab within the Products and Services section.
explanations.d: The Company tab stores basic company information; there is no Price Management section in the Company tab.

questions.name: Chart of Accounts & Products/Services
questions.keyword: Progress Invoicing enable and purpose
questions.text: A construction contractor using QuickBooks Online Plus wants to bill a client in stages as work is completed on a long project, starting from a single estimate. Their bookkeeper says this is possible with a specific feature. Where is progress invoicing enabled, and what does it allow?

answers.text: Enabled in Account and Settings > Advanced; allows splitting a single vendor bill into multiple staged payments
Enabled in Account and Settings > Expenses; allows contractors to track costs against a project budget over time
Enabled automatically when Projects is turned on; converts estimates to invoices by project completion percentage
Enabled in Account and Settings > Sales; allows creating multiple partial invoices from a single estimate

explanations.a: Progress invoicing is not in the Advanced tab and does not relate to splitting vendor bills; it is a sales-side feature for customer invoicing.
explanations.b: Progress invoicing is not in the Expenses tab; it is found in Account and Settings > Sales.
explanations.c: Progress invoicing must be explicitly enabled in Account and Settings > Sales; it is not automatically activated by turning on Projects.
explanations.d: Correct — Progress Invoicing is enabled in Account and Settings > Sales, and it allows users to create multiple partial invoices from a single estimate.
